name: Oxygeneo

card.summary: OxyGeneo is a facial treatment platform that combines exfoliation, topical infusion and oxygenation with TriPollar radiofrequency to improve skin texture, fine lines and pigmentation.
card.note: Clinic treatment; published data is a small pilot.

quick.overview:
OxyGeneo, delivered through the geneO+ platform from Pollogen of Tel Aviv, is a noninvasive facial that combines exfoliation, a topical infusion and oxygenation, with TriPollar radiofrequency used to warm the skin. It is also referred to as a carboxytherapy-style facial.

It is used to improve skin texture, fine lines and uneven pigmentation. The main published report is a small study of ten patients over eight weeks.
quick.how: A clinic delivers a series of weekly sessions. In the published study, six weekly treatments were given, with one of two topical infusions chosen for the person's skin concerns.
quick.risks: The published report describes it as noninvasive. Larger controlled trials were not found.

lead: OxyGeneo is a noninvasive skin treatment from the geneO+ platform by Pollogen Ltd. of Tel Aviv, Israel, which combines exfoliation, infusion and oxygenation through the Bohr effect with TriPollar radiofrequency.[1]

The rationale in a 2017 report is that skin oxygenation can improve cell growth and biosynthesis, which may improve appearance, while most oxygenation techniques are invasive.[1] In that study, ten patients with fine lines, wrinkles, hyperpigmentation and rough texture received six weekly treatments over two months; five had NeoRevive and five NeoBright topical infusions, and outcomes were assessed with VISIA complexion analysis and patient and evaluator surveys.[1] The report states results varied by patient.

chain: Smoother texture and more even tone
angle.text: A series of clinic sessions aims to improve skin texture, fine lines and pigmentation. Results in the published study were assessed over eight weeks.

paras: The treatment combines three steps in one platform: exfoliation, infusion of topical serums and oxygenation, together with TriPollar radiofrequency.[1]

A 2017 Journal of Clinical and Aesthetic Dermatology report enrolled ten patients with fine lines, wrinkles, hyperpigmentation and rough texture for six weekly treatments, using VISIA analysis and satisfaction surveys over eight weeks.[1]

timeline.event: Pilot study of OxyGeneo published in the Journal of Clinical and Aesthetic Dermatology.[1]

refs.title: Oxygeneo: A Unique Three-in-one Treatment of Exfoliation, Infusion, and Oxygenation via the Bohr Effect and TriPollar Radiofrequency for Skin Rejuvenation
